answer.rationale: Finance mandate requires an 18% cut and the incumbent has refused to reprice; the low-cost vendor alone meets the mandate. Before switching I want to confirm two inherited records: (1) memory_c2 — that onboarding and invoicing with the low-cost vendor were genuinely smooth last cycle, since a failed onboarding would jeopardize a 94%-utilization line, and (2) memory_c1 — that the incumbent relationship is otherwise stable, so I know what I am giving up (no migration cost, two-cycle stability) and that the incumbent refusal is indeed an impasse rather than negotiation theater. The constraint of one decision per cycle rules out add_second_source as an alternative; deferring risks the 14-day contract cliff; renegotiating is foreclosed by the incumbent refusal. Switching primary to the low-cost vendor, with a planned second-source addition next cycle, best minimizes TCO under the mandate while delivery risk is bounded by the verification of c2's onboarding record and the option to fall back on the incumbent's month-to-month terms if needed.
